intro: Power-user patterns that consistently produce better results from Claude Code.

items.title: CLAUDE.md is your force multiplier
items.body: Run /init once, edit the output, and every future session starts expert-in-context. Include commands, conventions, architecture, and gotchas. Update it as the project evolves.

items.title: Load context before asking
items.body: Type #src/lib/auth.ts before complex requests. Claude reads it immediately rather than spending a turn discovering it.

items.title: Be specific about scope
items.body: Vague: 'fix the bug'. Specific: 'fix the null pointer in src/api/auth.ts:47 when req.user is undefined'. Specific requests produce surgical edits.

items.title: One task at a time
items.body: Chain tasks explicitly with 'verify, then continue' rather than 'do steps 1–5 all at once'. You catch problems earlier and get better results at each step.

items.title: Verify before accepting
items.body: Always run: git diff (what changed?), npm test (still passing?), npm run lint (any regressions?). Don't trust the summary — read the diff.

items.title: Plan before implementing
items.body: For complex tasks: 'Don't write code yet — tell me your plan first.' This surfaces misunderstandings before they become wrong code.

items.title: Parallel agents with worktrees
items.body: Create git worktrees for independent features and run a Claude Code session in each. No file conflicts, full parallelism.

items.title: Hooks for automatic guardrails
items.body: Set up PostToolUse hooks to auto-run lint and type-check after every edit. Continuous feedback without asking for it.

items.title: The ! shortcut
items.body: Type ! command to run a shell command and pipe the output into the conversation. Great for feeding Claude real error messages or git log output.
